artworks.title: Halcyone
artworks.description: Draper's Edwardian Alcyone keeps vigil for Ceyx lost at sea — Ovid's widow before the gods turn both into halcyons.

artworks.title: Morpheus in the House of Ceyx, before Alcyone
artworks.description: Baur's Ovid etching: Morpheus wears the drowned king's face to Alcyone's sleep — the dream that reveals the wreck.

artworks.title: Alcyone and Ceyx Transformed into Halcyons
artworks.description: Picart's engraving of the climax: Alcyone finds Ceyx's body and both become kingfishers — the origin of the halcyon days.

artworks.title: Ceyx and Alcyone
artworks.description: A classic illustration of the Trachinian couple — married love that Ovid carries past shipwreck into birds and calm seas.

popCulture.title: Alcyone (mythology)
popCulture.description: Aeolus' daughter and Ceyx's wife — their sea-grief becomes the halcyon birds and the calm midwinter days.

popCulture.title: Ceyx
popCulture.description: The Trachinian king drowned on the voyage Alcyone begged him not to take — Ovid's emblem of married love past death.
